title: Learning Engineering: shared vocabulary and conceptual ontology
status: Working draft for community review; not an IEEE standard or an ICICLE-endorsed ontology
purpose: Help people across education, workplace learning, and other settings describe learning engineering consistently.

foundation.workingDefinition: Applying learning sciences through human-centered and engineering design, using iterative data-informed decisions to support learners and learning.
foundation.definitionStatus: Paraphrase of ICICLE's published definition, not a quotation

modelingConventions: All term definitions and relation labels below are proposed wording. Source references establish grounding, not endorsement.
Modules organize the vocabulary; they are not mutually exclusive categories or formal superclass axioms.
A relation describes a possible connection between instances of the named concepts. It is not mandatory for every instance.
Creation, implementation, investigation, and iteration can overlap. Their listing order does not prescribe a workflow.
Learning engineering has both process and practice aspects. Their distinction is a modeling choice, not a claim that ICICLE defines two separate entities.
Data, evidence, and decisions remain distinct. Observations do not automatically establish effectiveness or causation.
Desired outcomes and observed outcomes remain distinct. Intent does not establish achievement.
Learner and team-member terms describe participation roles. The same person may participate in several roles.
This draft specifies conceptual relationships, not formal OWL restrictions, cardinalities, or validation rules.

terms.label: Learning engineering
terms.definition: The process and practice characterized by the foundation definition above.

terms.label: Learning engineering process
terms.definition: Connected activities undertaken in a particular learning engineering effort.

terms.label: Learning engineering practice
terms.definition: The enacted use of learning engineering approaches across efforts.

terms.label: Learner
terms.definition: A participant whose learning the effort seeks to support.

terms.label: Stakeholder
terms.definition: A person or group with an interest in an effort.

terms.label: Learning context
terms.definition: Conditions surrounding learners, the challenge, and the solution.

terms.label: Learning challenge
terms.definition: A problem or opportunity an effort aims to address.

terms.label: Desired outcome
terms.definition: An intended result, distinguished from what actually occurs.

terms.label: Learning sciences
terms.definition: Scientific knowledge and inquiry concerning learning.

terms.label: Design principle
terms.definition: A statement guiding design choices under stated conditions.
terms.note: Candidate elaboration; inspect the listed Learning Design Principles toolkit.

terms.label: Design method
terms.definition: An approach for developing or revising a solution.

terms.label: Human-centered design method
terms.definition: A design method attending to people and their experience.

terms.label: Engineering design method
terms.definition: A design method for developing solutions against requirements and constraints.

terms.label: Learning solution
terms.definition: An arrangement intended to address a learning challenge.
terms.note: May combine instruction, support, activities, environments, and technology.

terms.label: Learning experience
terms.definition: An experience through which a learner engages in learning.

terms.label: Creation
terms.definition: Developing a solution, including design and instrumentation.

terms.label: Instrumentation
terms.definition: Establishing how observations will be defined and captured.

terms.label: Measurement
terms.definition: Assigning observations to defined measures using specified procedures.
terms.note: Distinguished from the wider work of instrumentation.

terms.label: Data
terms.definition: Recorded observations available for analysis.

terms.label: Evidence
terms.definition: Information interpreted as bearing on a question or claim.
terms.note: Proposed definition; inspect the listed Evidence Decision Tracker materials.

terms.label: Decision
terms.definition: A choice among actions, recorded with its rationale.
terms.note: Proposed definition; inspect the listed decision-tracking materials.

terms.label: Implementation
terms.definition: Putting a solution into use in its intended setting.

terms.label: Investigation
terms.definition: Examining data to understand results and inform further action.

terms.label: Observed outcome
terms.definition: A result observed during or after use of a solution.
terms.note: An observed result does not by itself establish causation.

terms.label: Iteration
terms.definition: Revisiting work and revising it in light of findings.

terms.label: Learning engineering team
terms.definition: People contributing expertise to a learning engineering effort.
terms.note: An effort may involve one person or several.

terms.label: Area of expertise
terms.definition: A domain of knowledge or skill contributed to an effort.

terms.label: Learning engineering adoption maturity
terms.definition: An organization's degree of adoption of learning engineering practices.
terms.note: Candidate elaboration; no maturity levels asserted before reviewing the listed model.

relationStatus: All relationships are proposed modeling choices, grounded in the cited vocabulary. They have not been validated as formal axioms.
competencyQuestions: Which challenge does an effort address, for which learners, and in which context?
Which learning-science knowledge and design methods inform the effort?
Which desired outcomes motivated a solution, and which outcomes were actually observed?
How were observations captured and interpreted as evidence for a decision?
What did an iteration change, why, and with whose participation?
Which expertise contributed to the effort?

illustrativeCase.status: Invented example, not empirical evidence or an ICICLE case
illustrativeCase.challenge: New employees have difficulty completing a troubleshooting task.
illustrativeCase.context: Workplace onboarding with supervised access to equipment.
illustrativeCase.desiredOutcome: Employees complete the task independently and correctly.
illustrativeCase.solution: A guided simulation followed by supervised practice.
illustrativeCase.instrumentation: Define task-success criteria and collect attempts and rubric ratings.
illustrativeCase.observedOutcome: Some participants still omit a diagnostic check.
illustrativeCase.evidence: The recurring omission suggests a candidate weakness to investigate; it does not establish its cause.
illustrativeCase.decision: Revise the relevant practice activity and examine subsequent performance.
illustrativeCase.iteration: Introduce the revised activity while preserving comparable measurement procedures.

openModelingQuestions: Should knowledge, claims, measures, instruments, and decision rationales become separately defined concepts?
How should an effort represent multiple iterations and changing context over time?
Which relations need qualifiers for time, uncertainty, evidence quality, or provenance?
Which extensions are needed for technology standards, accessibility, ethics, and organizational adoption?
Would the community prefer a controlled vocabulary first, followed by a formally constrained ontology?
